problem.title: Foreign creditors in Brazil are powerless
problem.sub: Without local presence, CPF/CNPJ or a Brazilian lawyer, you can't use the tools that actually pressure a debtor in Brazil.
problem.card1desc: Only companies with a Brazilian CNPJ can add debtors to credit bureaus. Your name, however legitimate, generates no pressure on the Brazilian debtor.
problem.card2desc: Protesting titles in Brazil requires a local legal representative. Without one, you can't register the default at a notary — and the debtor knows it.
problem.card3desc: Filing a lawsuit in Brazil as a foreign creditor is expensive, takes years and requires a bond deposit. In practice, it's unfeasible for most credits.

solution.title: How CrossCollect works
solution.sub: In 4 steps, we turn your international credit into real payment.
solution.step1desc: In 4 steps you register the debtor, the amount in foreign currency and the supporting documentation.
solution.step2desc: Automatic emails and WhatsApps in Portuguese, with progressively formal tone, on days 1, 7, 15 and 30.
solution.step3desc: If there's no response, we blacklist the CPF/CNPJ on Serasa Experian and protest the title at a notary office.
solution.step4desc: When payment occurs, we forward the amount in USD, EUR or GBP via international wire transfer.
solution.ctasub: Free for up to 5 debts · No credit card
